review_note: Cosmogonic/philosophical principle (Samkhya); no astronomical counterpart.

aksha = terrestrial latitude. Draft 'componential' came only from the two-word gloss. FLAG for v1.1: variants lamba/lambaka are CO-latitude, as the corpus itself shows at 3.14 'co-latitude (lamba) and of latitude (aksha)' and 12.44 'co-latitude (lambaka)'. They are kept only because the glossary is frozen.
Two distinct senses: a linear unit (digit / finger-breadth) and graduated divisions on an instrument.
apakrama and kranti both map to declination.
'setting' and the narrower 'heliacal setting' are both cited senses.
Mythological being; no astronomical counterpart.
Parallax resolved into its latitude component (the longitude component is lambana).

Solstice, the sun's northward/southward progress, and precession (ayanamsa) are all cited senses. Reviewer S proposed 'precession' as the primary gloss; adjudicated KEEP 'solstice' as primary (4 of 6 verses print solstice), with precession kept in other_glosses.
bha (asterism) + cakra (circle) = circle of asterisms (ecliptic band). It overlaps with bhagana's 'circle of constellations' sense.
Revolution count vs circle of constellations/zodiac; senses depend on context.
Arc 'portion' of an asterism (nakshatra division of 800'); there is no modern unit for it, and 'portion' is Burgess's generic rendering. Draft 'one_to_many' came only from the plural 'portions'.
Base (side) of a right triangle; a single sense.
Religious/metaphysical concept.
Projection (diagram) of an eclipse.
sighra (the 'swift' epicycle/conjunction) models synodic anomaly, which modern astronomy explains by heliocentric geometry. 'Conjunction' is shared with cighrocca, samagama and yoga.
Conjunction-apex of the sighra epicycle, listed separately from mandocca and pata in the source. It belongs to the epicyclic model, so it has no direct modern counterpart.
Additive (+) in a correction; 'excess' and 'additive' are the same sense. Draft 'one_to_many' came from the row's shape.
Fixed (karanas), polar longitude, pole and pole-star are distinct context-dependent senses.
Gnomon (sanku); the 'ganku' form is OCR for c-cedilla.
Obscuration (eclipsed amount).
preceptor/master in the cited verses; guru also names Jupiter elsewhere in the tradition, so expansions are ambiguous.
Hour. Draft 'one_to_many' came only from the plural. (The hora = half-sign sense is not cited here.)
Orbit.
Anomaly, distance and commutation are cited senses.
Perpendicular (upright side) of a right triangle.
kranti and apakrama both map to declination.
Horizon.
Orient ecliptic-point: the point of the ecliptic on the eastern horizon (ascendant), composed from the ecliptic and the horizon.
Cited verses use 'meridian', but madhya is overwhelmingly 'mean' (madhyama graha) in planetary theory. Confidence lowered because expansion risks pulling in mean-motion verses.
Measure / dimensions / the modes of measuring time.
Slow (manda) epicycle apsis, an epicyclic model of the equation of centre. 'Apsis' is shared with mandocca and ucca.
Apex of the manda epicycle. It corresponds to apsis/apogee but sits inside an epicyclic model. Draft 'many_to_one' kept as the secondary type.
Mythological patriarch.
Cosmological time cycle (age of a Manu); no astronomical counterpart.
Lunar mansion: both a star group and a fixed 13°20' ecliptic division. Modern 'asterism' covers only the first. Draft 'one_to_many' came only from the plural.
Quadrant vs fourth part/quarter (e.g. of an asterism).
Node (1.33) vs astronomical aspect (ch. 11); compound-specific 'fault' at 11.4.
Provector: a cosmic wind that drives diurnal motion. The phenomenon (diurnal rotation) is real, but the causal model differs completely.
Conjunction; shared with cighra/cighrocca/yoga.
Aggregate circle (radius = half the sum of the eclipsed and eclipsing diameters).
Entrance into a sign (ingress): entrance + sign.
Solar (time measure).
Civil (sunrise-to-sunrise) day. Draft 'one_to_many' came only from 'civil days'. Note: the modern civil day starts at midnight.
Perfected beings (mythological).
True/corrected (vs mean) position. 'corrected', 'true' and 'precise' are translation variants of a single sense.
(Half-)duration of an eclipse.
Gods (mythological).
'Darkness' = the eclipsing shadow (umbra), framed as darkness and not as a geometric shadow cone.
Apsis/apex of an epicycle (epicyclic model); shared 'apsis' with manda/mandocca.
Altitude (in time) vs elevated/erect (instrumental sense).
'Deflection' of the ecliptic from the east-west line at the eclipsed body. It is used for drawing eclipse projections, and Burgess's term has no exact modern counterpart.
Scripture.
Second (of arc). Draft 'one_to_many' came only from plural/filler forms.
Equinox vs equator (context-dependent).
Conjunction (shared with cighra/cighrocca/samagama); yoga is ALSO the calendrical yoga (sum of solar and lunar longitudes, 2.65). Confidence lowered for that ambiguity.
Planetary 'war' = close conjunction/appulse of two planets, framed as a combat.

Cosmological age (13.18 prints 'successive age (yuga)'). Reviewer S proposed 'epoch' and is CORRECT for 1.56, which prints 'any epoch (yuga)'. The glossary note 'epoch unsupported' is wrong for that verse. Glossary frozen, so no edit: FLAG for v1.1 (add 'epoch' to other_glosses). Confidence stays Low.
